description: Sliding-window hydropathy/hydrophobicity profile (ProtScale-style) over a published amino-acid scale. On the Kyte-Doolittle scale it also returns `hydrophobicStretches`: spans where the 19-residue average stays at or above 1.6, the line Kyte & Doolittle (1982) draw for a membrane-buried segment. ⚠️ That is a FACT ABOUT THE CURVE, not a transmembrane prediction — it cannot tell a signal peptide's h-region from a membrane helix, carries no inside/outside topology, and fires on a buried hydrophobic core in a soluble protein. For an actual prediction use protein_annotate_submit, whose InterProScan run includes Phobius, TMHMM and SignalP.

scale.description: Amino-acid scale. Kyte-Doolittle and Eisenberg are hydrophobicity; Hopp-Woods is hydrophilicity.

sequence.description: Protein sequence (one-letter amino-acid codes; non-AA characters ignored).

window.description: Sliding-window size (clamped to an odd number ≥ 1). Affects the PROFILE only: `hydrophobicStretches` is always measured at window 19, because the 1.6 line is calibrated against that window and would otherwise report the plot's smoothing rather than the sequence.

name: protein_hydrophobicity
title: Hydrophobicity Profile
